question: Which of the following can be blocked by atropine, a muscarinic receptor blocker?

options.opa: Increased blood pressure caused by nicotine
options.opb: Increased skeletal muscle strength caused by neostigmine, an acetycholine esterase inhibitor
options.opc: Bradycardia caused by infusion of acetylcholine

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors" -> "Inhibition of acetylcholine effects" -> "Prevention of bradycardia caused by acetylcholine" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors" -> "Inhibition of parasympathetic nervous system" -> "Possible increase in heart rate" -> "Does not affect nicotine-induced blood pressure increase" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors" -> "Inhibition of neostigmine effects" -> "Decreased skeletal muscle strength" -> "Unclear if this is significant" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors" -> "Inhibition of acetylcholine effects" -> "Prevention of bradycardia caused by acetylcholine" -> "Does not block nicotine effects" -> "Does not block neostigmine effects" -> "Not all options are blocked" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors" -> "Inhibition of acetylcholine effects" -> "Prevention of bradycardia caused by acetylcholine" -> "Does not affect nicotine-induced blood pressure increase" -> "Does not affect neostigmine-induced muscle strength" -> "Only bradycardia is blocked" -> 90%
analysis: Atropine is a muscarinic receptor antagonist that blocks the effects of acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors. It can effectively counteract bradycardia caused by acetylcholine infusion (option c). However, it does not block increased blood pressure caused by nicotine (option a) or increased skeletal muscle strength caused by neostigmine (option b), as these effects are mediated through different mechanisms. Therefore, the correct answer is only option c, not all of them.
